question: In a water-drive reservoir, what aquifer process can supply expansion energy as oil is produced? Cite the internal source.
reference_answer: Expansion of water in the connected aquifer can drive reservoir fluids during production.
agent_answer:
In a water-drive reservoir, the aquifer process that can supply expansion energy as oil is produced is the compressibility of the aquifer system. [KB3]
The effectiveness of water drive depends on the ability of the aquifer to replace the volume of the produced oil. [KB3]
The key issues with a water drive reservoir are the size of the aquifer and permeability. [KB3]
The expansion of the aquifer into the depleting oil zone in the reservoir will lead to a steady elevation in the oil water contact (OWC). [KB4]
Water drive is frequently encountered as a naturally occurring drive mechanism. [KB4]
review_note: The answer matches the source’s statement that water-drive energy comes from aquifer water expansion/compressibility.

question: A well has positive skin after completion. Explain what this suggests near the wellbore and why a poorly designed matrix treatment could make matters worse.
reference_answer: Positive skin suggests reduced near-well permeability/formation damage. A treatment can mobilize fines or create a water block, further restricting flow.
agent_answer:
A well has positive skin after completion. This suggests that there is a localized reduction in permeability near the wellbore, which increases the pressure drop in the vicinity of the well. [KB3]
A poorly designed matrix treatment could make matters worse because it may cause additional formation damage, leading to a further reduction in permeability near the wellbore. [KB3] [KB4]
The positive skin factor indicates that the permeability around the well has been reduced, which can be caused by drilling and completion activities or formation damage. [KB3]
Formation damage near the completion face can significantly increase the additional pressure drop and thus the calculated skin factor. [KB4]
